request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: an explainable boosting machine (EBM), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 36.4% (95% band 29.9% to 48.9%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.4; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.42, 95% band [+2.15, +2.69]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 21.9% (95% band 16.0% to 26.4%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 94999: +0.38; >= 95000: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.06, 95% band [-1.40, -0.61]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 11.6% (95% band 7.8% to 17.6%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2658: +0.1; >= 2659: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.60, 95% band [-0.93, -0.31]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.6% (95% band 0.8% to 9.9%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.24, 95% band [-0.48, +0.06]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.5% (95% band 0.9% to 7.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.08, 95% band [-0.17, +0.26]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 4.5% (95% band 1.3% to 8.0%); rank 4 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.35 (95% band [+0.02, +0.61]) from x = 23 (5th percentile) to x = 53 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.4% (95% band 0.6% to 8.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.24, 95% band [-0.04, +0.45]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.3% (95% band 0.5% to 6.5%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.09, 95% band [-0.20, +0.28]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.0% to 4.4%); rank 6 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.03, 95% band [-0.13, +0.06]).

Interactions: the model has 5 pairs. The larger ones:
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.06 (95% band -1.42 to -0.63) when `AGE` = 23, -1.24 (95% band -1.66 to -0.67) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.43 (95% band +0.02 to +0.67) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.24 (95% band -0.06 to +0.60) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 1.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.8%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.93 (95% band -1.34 to -0.50) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -1.12 (95% band -1.58 to -0.70) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: +0.24 (95% band -0.11 to +0.54) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.05 (95% band -0.40 to +0.23) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT2 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 1.6% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: -0.01 (95% band -0.42 to +0.25) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -0.34 (95% band -0.55 to +0.03) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: +0.13 (95% band -0.19 to +0.28) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -0.20 (95% band -0.49 to +0.21) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.0% to 1.9%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.19 (95% band -0.05 to +0.45) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.26 (95% band -0.05 to +0.53) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: -0.18 (95% band -0.54 to +0.10) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.11 (95% band -0.45 to +0.11) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.3%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.96 (95% band -1.40 to -0.61) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -1.76 (95% band -2.04 to -0.61) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: +0.73 (95% band -0.14 to +1.01) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.07 (95% band -0.33 to +0.26) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by the applicant's most recent repayment status, PAY_0, which accounts for about 36% of the model's importance; an applicant who was 2 or more months behind in September 2005 is much more likely to default, with a logit contribution of about +2 compared with about -0.4 for those paid in full."},{"id":2,"text":"The size of the credit limit, LIMIT_BAL, is the second most important driver at about 22%, and it works in the opposite direction: applicants with limits of 95,000 NT dollars or more carry lower default risk than those below that level, with a net change of about -1.06 across the typical range."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in September 2005, PAY_AMT1, is the third driver at about 12%, with larger payments associated with lower risk (net change of about -0.60 across the typical range), though its band is fairly wide."},{"id":4,"text":"Other variables matter less: AGE shows a modest rise in risk with older age (about +0.35 across the typical range, with an uncertain shape), and the earlier payment amounts, bill amounts and education contribute little whose effect the data resolve clearly."},{"id":5,"text":"The model contains some interactions, most notably between credit limit and age, between credit limit and the July payment, and between credit limit and the August bill amount; the strongest of these is only about 2% of importance and its effect bands are wide, so the data do not settle how large these interactions are in practice."},{"id":6,"text":"The importance estimates themselves are uncertain, as the bands for the lower-ranked features overlap considerably, so the ordering beyond the top two or three drivers should be read cautiously."}]}
